Prevention: Crop rotation with fodder crops such as
Clean all equipment, tools and stakes used in an infested field before using in non-infested field.
Maintain proper plant to plant (9 in) and row to row distance (2.5 feet).
Proper land levelling to avoid severe dry or wet conditions in field.
Manual seed cleaning, to remove plant debris to prevent carry-over of the fungus.
Avoid working when plants are wet.
Monitoring: Watch out for leaf spot disease in early dry season or in rainy season as that offer ideal environment for the spread of disease.
Disease begins as small, lighter coloured areas, almost yellow.
Later they become bronze to dark grey, roughly circular to more elongated.
Dead areas fall out, giving a shot-hole appearance.
Direct Control: Neem leaf extract, Datura leaf extract, Garlic clove extract, Arjun leaf extract, Aswagandha leaf extract and
Aloe vera leaf extract @ 10% provides moderate protection against this disease.
Remove diseased leaves or plants and bury them in the soil to avoid further spread.
Treat the seed with hot water at 52 °C for 8 minutes provides protection against this disease.
Restrictions: Keep pesticides out of reach of children.
Always wear protective clothing, such as mask, rubber boots and gloves.
Dispose of containers responsibly (do not clean containers in canals).
Fungicides may be applied on a 7-day schedule, if necessary.
For all fungicides, thorough coverage of foliage is important for the control disease.
